newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ryanair flights add discount cargo space ex-Sweden.
newsitem.headline: Ryanair flights add discount cargo space ex-Sweden.

text.p: Irish airline Ryanair's new passenger flights will add some 90 tonnes of freight capacity from Sweden per month and it may be offered at discount rates, a spokesman for the airline's cargo operations said on Thursday.

Ryanair on Thursday began flying a Boeing 737 with a cargo capacity of 1,500 kg twice daily between Skavsta airport 100 kms southwest of Stockholm and London's Stansted. Pace Airline Services will be selling the belly capacity on the flights.
Malcolm Warner, managing director at Pace, said Pace would buy all the space on the Ryanair flights from Skavsta, which would amount to 90 tonnes per month.
He said pricing on freight would probably reflect the airline's policy for its passenger side. Ryanair, a no-frills airline, offers discount fares from smaller airports.
"I would imagine so. That's the way we operate. I need to fill those flights no matter what because I am paying for them," Warner told Reuters.
There had been good market response for the added capacity from London to Stockholm, Warner said. He said there was also a need for capacity between Sweden and Ireland.
"I don't think there is any capacity between Sweden and Dublin for instance. The Swedish market is mainly electronics so we'll hopefully take some of that," he said.
Pace appointed a representative -- Air Consultants of Malmo, Sweden -- to sell the space to freight forwarders, he said.
